titulo_es.@es: Consejo con ought to y obligación pasada con had to
titulo_es.@en: Council with regard to and obligation

consejo.@es: Va seguido de un verbo en forma base.
consejo.@en: It is followed by a verb in base form.

policy.es: política; plan o conjunto de normas oficiales

texto.@es: **Ought to + verbo** expresa una recomendación, como **should**. **Ought to** suele ser más formal y **should** es más frecuente: **You ought to rest** = Deberías descansar. La forma negativa **ought not to** existe; en conversación suele ser más común **shouldn't**.
texto.@en: **Ought to + verbo** expresses a recommendation, such as **should**. **Ought to** is usually more formal and **should** is more common: **You ought to rest** = You should rest. The negative form **ought not to** exists; in conversation it is usually more common **shouldn't**.

texto.@es: **Had to + verbo** expresa una obligación o necesidad pasada: **Mia had to work yesterday**. En negativa, **didn't have to + verbo** significa que no era necesario hacerlo; no significa que estuviera prohibido. **Mustn't** expresa que algo está prohibido (por ejemplo, según una norma vigente). Para una prohibición pasada, es claro usar **wasn't/weren't allowed to**; **couldn't** también puede expresar que no estaba permitido si el contexto lo deja claro.
texto.@en: **Had to + verbo** expresses a past obligation or necessity: **Mia had to work yesterday**. In negative, **didn't have to + verbo** means that it was not necessary to do so; it does not mean that it was prohibited. **Mustn't** states that something is prohibited (for example, according to an existing rule). For a past ban, it is clear to use **wasn't/weren't allowed to**; **couldn't** can also express that it was not allowed if the context makes it clear.

texto.@es: **Policy** es una política, un plan o un conjunto de normas oficiales; puede referirse a una empresa o a un gobierno (**government policy** = política del gobierno). **Politics** es la actividad política o el estudio de la política. La traducción depende del contexto: **policy** no es simplemente «lo contrario de politics».
texto.@en: **Policy** is a policy, a plan or a set of official rules; it may refer to a company or a government (**government policy** = government policy). **Politics** is the political activity or the study of politics. The translation depends on the context: **policy** is not simply «lo contrario de politics».

frases.en: Mia is an employee at a small design company.

analisis.@en: had to end; expresses a past obligation

frases.en: She still had to do the shopping.

frases.en: Washing her uniform was another chore.
frases.es: Lavar el uniforme fue otro quehacer.

frases.en: Her friend says, “You ought to rest tonight.”

analisis.@en: should rest; it is a council

frases.en: Mia doesn't have to work tomorrow, so she can rest.
frases.es: Mia no tiene que trabajar mañana, así que puede descansar.

analisis.@es: no es necesario; aquí se refiere al presente
analisis.@en: not necessary; here is the present

analisis.@en: employer; policy = official policy or rules of the company
